title: The public API omits its own escape hatch
sourceNote: Published type declarations, verifiable with `npm pack @zentauri-ui/zentauri-components`.
caption: CopyButton is one of the library's simplest components, which is why it shows the API decision clearly: the base props carry a render seam, and the type the consumer actually receives has it removed.

notes.text: The last line is the whole decision. `renderIcon` exists so the animated build can swap static icons for motion ones — but it is implementation detail, so the exported `CopyButtonProps` subtracts it. A consumer cannot reach the seam, and the seam can change without a breaking release.
`timeout` documents its own edge case in the type, rather than leaving `0` to be discovered. Every prop here carries a doc comment, which is what makes the surface usable without reading the source.

Extending `ComponentPropsWithRef<'button'>` and omitting only the two props it redefines means `type`, `disabled`, `aria-*` and `ref` all keep working. The component adds behaviour without taking anything away.

title: Motion is a separate entry point, not a prop
sourceNote: Published type declarations. The static and animated barrels are separate module paths.
caption: The claim "motion is optional" is usually a prop that ships the animation library to everyone anyway. Here it is enforced by module boundary: `framer-motion` is imported in the animated subpath and nowhere else.

notes.text: `framer-motion` appears in the animated subpath's types and not in the static one. Import `ui/copy-button` and the animation library is not in your graph at all — the cost follows the import, not the install.

The animated props are the static props *plus one*. There is no second API to learn and no divergence to maintain: swapping `CopyButton` for `CopyButtonAnimated` is a one-word change at the call site.

Three named presets rather than an open transition object. The consumer picks an intent; the library owns the timing. This is the same reason this site exposes `--ease-*` tokens instead of raw cubic-béziers.

title: A gate that makes one green check mean one specific thing
sourceNote: Runs on every `pnpm verify`. The excerpt is the assertion block, lightly trimmed.
caption: The suite behind I-02 is not public, so here is the same discipline applied to this site, where you can read the whole file. This site's riskiest claim is that its 3D layer is removable without loss. That claim is a test, not a promise.

notes.text: Asserting *absence* turned out to be stronger than the original plan, which only asked for `aria-hidden`. The scene renders null on the server, so a visitor with no JavaScript, no WebGL, or a `saveData` connection never receives the element at all.

The source-level sweep is the part that catches the real failure mode. A canvas is easy to keep accessible on day one; the risk is interactivity slowly migrating into it over months. This fails the build the first time a `<button>` appears in the scene tree.
Two separate budget facts, asserted separately: the 233KB scene chunk is allowed to be large precisely because this proves it is not on the critical path, which stayed at 2.4KB across three phases.
